messages:
Maya Chen: FYI support ticket #CS-8912 — Acme reported that their rerank endpoint is returning different scores after last night's model push. Same request input, different scores across calls. They also hit a 400 once with 'invalid input format'.
Alejandra Ruiz: Thanks Maya. Can you paste the original request and the differing responses? Also any request_id from their 400?
Maya Chen: Pasted below (redacted customer IDs). They included two request_ids: req_20260315_01 and req_20260315_02. Payload:```json
{
  "query": "best italian restaurants near me",
  "candidates": ["Luigi's Trattoria", "Pasta House", "Trattoria Bella"],
  "top_k": 3
}```
Response A (req_20260315_01): scores [0.92, 0.54, 0.31]
Response B (req_20260315_02): scores [0.67, 0.88, 0.25]
Maya Chen: The 400 happened on a third call where they had a trailing comma in the JSON: "candidates": ["A","B",], — per their logs. They fixed it client-side but want assurance this isn't a server parsing regression.
Devon Park: @Maya can you forward the raw headers for the two successful calls? Need model version, route, and latency. Also did they specify a model override param?
Maya Chen: Headers (redacted): model: rerank-v2.3.1, route: /v1/rerank, latency: 123ms vs 118ms. No model_override param present.
Samir Patel: Noting rerank-v2.3.1 was rolled out to canary yesterday at 23:10 UTC and promoted to prod at 02:04 UTC. @deploy-bot can you confirm?
deploy-bot: Deployment report — canary deploy of rerank-v2.3.1 started 2026-03-15T23:10:07Z. Production promotion completed 2026-03-16T02:04:12Z. No rollback.
Devon Park: OK. Two hypotheses: 1) Non-determinism in ranking due to sampling/temperature; 2) Model param or metadata ordering dependence; 3) Bug in server-side tokenization for certain input shapes. Need reproducible test.
Alejandra Ruiz: Customer says they re-run same payload 5 times and scores flipped on 2 runs. They can share full request bodies/timestamps if we need.
Samir Patel: Eng-ML, any known nondeterminism introduced in 2.3.1? We added a new attention fusion that shouldn't affect deterministic outputs, but maybe kv-cache or batching changed ordering.
Eng-ML Bot: Change log for rerank-v2.3.1: quantization tweak (int8 fastpath), microbatching optimization, tokenizer update (unicode normalization fix).
Devon Park: Tokenizer update is suspicious. If unicode normalization changed token boundaries, identical strings could produce different tokenization depending on pre-normalized bytes (e.g., invisible trailing spaces). Ask customer to md5 their raw request body bytes.
Maya Chen: I've asked customer to send raw bodies + md5s. Meanwhile I'll try to repro internally using both old and new tokenizer settings.
Samir Patel: Also check server logs for parse errors correlated to the 400. The trailing-comma should be a client-side JSON parse error, but we shouldn't crash; we should return 400 without changing rerank state.
Devon Park: Quick repro attempt: I ran the payload locally against both v2.3.0 and v2.3.1 containers. v2.3.0 scores [0.91, 0.53, 0.32], v2.3.1 scores [0.68, 0.87, 0.25] — reproduced.
Devon Park: Dumping tokenization diff:```
v2.3.0 tokens: ["best","italian","restaurants","near","me"]
v2.3.1 tokens: ["best","italian","restaurants","near","me"]
```
Devon Park: Tokenization looks identical for this example. Next: compare logits before softmax.
Alejandra Ruiz: Any quick mitigation we can offer Acme while this is triaged? Can we pin them to v2.3.0?
Samir Patel: Yes — we can add a per-customer model pin. Ops: can you create a temp route mapping for Acme to rerank-v2.3.0 (no config changes) and TTL 72h? @devon will validate.
Devon Park: Created route acme-rerank-pin -> rerank-v2.3.0. Will validate after warmup.
Maya Chen: Customer confirmed they can be pinned. They asked for a writeup of the root cause and a plan.
Devon Park: Root cause preliminary: score divergence due to a change in candidate representation ordering in the batching optimizer. We had a microbatch reorder to improve GPU utilization; it changed candidate relative positions during attention masking leading to different logits order in some edge cases when candidate list lengths vary and padding is applied. The bug: mask indexing used inplace reindex that depended on original candidate buffer address.
Eng-ML Bot: Alert: batching-optimizer microbatch reindex change committed in PR #4821. Assigned to @Samir.
Samir Patel: Confirmed. I have a failing unit test that demonstrates the incorrect mask alignment for variable candidate lengths. Patch incoming. Will run canary revert if needed.
Devon Park: Action items: 1) Keep Acme pinned to v2.3.0 (ops) — DONE. 2) Samir to hotfix batching mask and run internal eval on a representative prompt set. 3) QA to run A/B on 50k sample rerank pairs to quantify score drift. 4) Product/customer-success to draft incident note and customer communication.
Alejandra Ruiz: I'll draft the customer note: explain cause, show example diffs, apologies, and ETA for fix. Also offer free credits if they incurred regressions.
Samir Patel: Patch landed in branch fix/batching-mask-4821, running CI. If green, I'll cut v2.3.2 canary.
deploy-bot: CI: all tests passed for fix/batching-mask-4821. Can deploy to canary on request.
Devon Park: Before canary, run deterministic regression suite (5k inputs) to validate no other regressions. I'll run that now.
Maya Chen: Customer updated: they saw ~3% of rerank calls change top-1 after yesterday's deploy. They're OK with temporary pin but ask for root cause doc when available.
Devon Park: Regression suite run complete: on our dataset, v2.3.1 vs v2.3.0 shows 2.8% top-1 flips. v2.3.2 (patched) vs v2.3.0 shows 0.2% flips. Looks good.
Samir Patel: Rolling v2.3.2 to canary at 2026-03-16T12:34:00Z.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy of rerank-v2.3.2 started.
Maya Chen: I'll send the draft to Acme and let them know about the pin and the upcoming fix.
Alejandra Ruiz: Customer reply: they repro'd the flip earlier but after pinning to v2.3.0 they get consistent scores. They're very appreciative. :thumbsup:
Devon Park: Closing loop: root cause = batching optimizer reindex bug causing mask misalignment -> score instability. Fix = correct reindex and add unit test + regression suite. Postmortem and release notes to be prepared.
Maya Chen: Thanks team. Logging this thread to CS ticket and will attach test diffs.
Samir Patel: I'll follow up with a short writeup for the postmortem.
Eng-ML Bot: Postmortem checklist: assign author, timeline, impact, mitigation, permanent fix, tests added.
Maya Chen: Thread closed for now.
